CLOUD REVIEWER seat for PR #2469 of tvofi/heatpump_optimizer, at head 67ee6adfd712786da12241bf59bb5b78030c2d80. Bus nonce: 1808b2e15cb51d3f259ff03e92c6a423. Never send push notifications.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md and its rules from main, and follow them exactly. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin 67ee6adfd712786da12241bf59bb5b78030c2d80`; the PR body is in the PR. Verify each claim adversarially: mutate the fix and check the tests fail, and check every figure in the body at this head. Check that it merges with origin/main (`git merge-tree --write-tree`) and read CI on this head from the check-runs API.
Output: in a fresh directory of your own (`W=$(mktemp -d)`), write verdict.md, whose first line is exactly `Fix review: merge 67ee6adfd712786da12241bf59bb5b78030c2d80` or `Fix review: blocked 67ee6adfd712786da12241bf59bb5b78030c2d80 <class>: <reason>` (no brackets; the class is lower-case letters and dashes), in the format the role file gives, then a blank line, then `bus-nonce: 1808b2e15cb51d3f259ff03e92c6a423`; put the evidence in `ev/` beside it. Do NOT run bus.sh: its dispatch record lives on the orchestrator's machine, which publishes the verdict there (cloud_relay.sh). Return the verdict on a probe ref, and push nothing else; this builds one parentless commit with a private index and touches no branch of your checkout: `R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); G=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir); mkdir -p $W/pr && cp -r $W/verdict.md $W/ev $W/pr/ && cd $W/pr && T=$(GIT_DIR=$G GIT_INDEX_FILE=$W/idx GIT_WORK_TREE=$W/pr sh -c 'git add -A -f . && git write-tree') && C=$(GIT_DIR=$G git -c user.name=seat -c user.email=seat@users.noreply.github.com commit-tree $T -m "verdict 2469 67ee6adfd712786da12241bf59bb5b78030c2d80") && git -C $R push -q origin $C:refs/heads/probe/rev-2469-1808b2e1`. That ref is the return signal. Do not post comments, approve or merge.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
Round 5 of R10-UPDATE-PR-LOCK, at head 67ee6adf (code 931e9a0f). This is the SPLIT that the three-round rule required after round 4 at 98fe31c2 was blocked flaky-arm. In that round, the SIGKILL arm failed 7/7 in the cloud container, because of late orphan reaping.

This PR keeps only mechanisms whose arms are deterministic. Each one has the revert that fails it:
- lock and BUSY 75: mut:lock
- EXIT-trap release: mut:unlock
- the TERM/INT/HUP trap (it runs after the foreground push, so kill <pid> frees the lock only after the push): mut:stop
- the holder lives while its parent does: mut:watch
- no stale lock after a SIGKILL: a hand-applied while True
- no lock fd in the shell: round 0's shell-fd version
- relay body dir: the base mktemp line
- relay cleanup: rm -rf deleted
- relay retry on 75: the urc=75 line deleted

These moved out to R10-UPDATE-PR-SIGNALS, now on main via roster #2475 (merged 1e30f876), through three Carry: lines:
- the group drain;
- the process-group re-exec, which also removes the ps dependency;
- mut:drain, mut:pgrp and mut:holdgrp.

Every wait in the arms is on a condition with a generous bound. The fixer's claim is that none depends on reaping speed, because the kernel frees a flock when the holder exits, not when it is reaped. Self-tests on macOS: pr_args 56/0 on 8/8 runs, 3 of them in parallel under load; cloud_relay 74/0. The fixer had no container.

RUN THE SELF-TESTS IN YOUR CLOUD CONTAINER at least 5 times and report N/N. Round 4 failed exactly there.

Also verify:
- every mutant and revert above;
- that the moved mechanisms are gone;
- carry_audit, which should route 3/3 against origin/main;
- CI from the check-runs API;
- the merge with origin/main.

Say that this is round 5, the split.
